paper_metadata.title: Quantum Risk Analysis of Financial Derivatives

summary: The paper proposes two gate-based quantum algorithms for estimating portfolio Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Conditional VaR: a QAE-based method and a QSP-based method. Numerical simulations show the QSP approach requires about 10× fewer oracle calls than the QAE variant for the same VaR error, and resource estimates suggest VaR estimation could reduce the logical clock rate needed for quantum advantage in derivative pricing by up to ~30× under favorable assumptions (e.g., ~50k scenarios).

experiments.description: QAE-based value-at-risk estimation for derivative portfolios using a superposition over market scenarios and coherent amplitude estimation to compare portfolio values against a VaR threshold.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) VaR for derivative portfolios
algorithm.convergence_criteria: bisection search over threshold µ until estimated P[V ≤ µ] reaches 1-α within target amplitude-estimation accuracy
algorithm.parameter_initialization: bisection initialized with µ_l=0 and µ_h=1

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Scenario register |s⟩ encodes market tweaks; derivative value V(s) is encoded as an amplitude via oracle A, then compared to threshold µ using a binary comparator
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate VaR_α[V] = V0 - µ_α where µ_α is the smallest threshold such that P[V ≤ µ_α] ≥ 1-α
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Binary comparator C_µ and QAE-based probability estimation; no optimization constraints

problem_instance.description: Derivative portfolio risk estimation over multiple market scenarios; benchmarked on simulated scenario prices drawn from a normal distribution for numerical studies

dataset_specification.description: Scenario prices sampled from N(µ=0.5, σ^2=0.09^2) for numerical experiments; also discussed as general market-scenario loading

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Scenario values normalized to [0,1]; portfolio prices under scenarios are encoded coherently
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 100 independent samples per data point for numerical error plots; 200 repetitions for advantage benchmark; bisection search over µ with QAE at each step

implementation_details.classical_solver: classical Monte Carlo / sorting for baseline and comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Generate scenario prices; sort classical samples to obtain baseline VaR
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare quantum VaR estimate to classical percentile estimate

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: bisection-based threshold search; no training loss

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Requires coherent derivative pricing oracle A plus nested QAE; oracle-call complexity N_QAE_μ(m) = 2^m + 1 per threshold evaluation and repeated QAE rounds within bisection search.
limiting_factors: Quadratic speedup only (amplitude estimation vs Monte Carlo)

Need for high-precision derivative pricing oracle
Scenario superposition preparation not demonstrated at scale
Numerical experiments performed via classical simulation only

notes: No physical QPU or simulator platform is named for the numerical experiments; treated as simulator_other because the paper reports explicit numerical simulations of the algorithm rather than hardware execution.
The paper gives resource formulas and oracle-call counts, but not a concrete total qubit count or depth for a specific instance; num_qubits and circuit_depth are therefore left null.
Paper analyzes asymptotic scaling and performs numerical simulations but does not execute the algorithm on quantum hardware.
No empirical demonstration of outperforming classical VaR estimation; analysis remains theoretical.

experiments.description: QSP-based value-at-risk estimation for derivative portfolios using a block-encoded pricing oracle and polynomial threshold approximation, followed by QAE to read out the threshold probability.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Signal Processing (QSP) VaR for derivative portfolios with polynomial threshold approximation
algorithm.convergence_criteria: bisection search over threshold µ until estimated P[V ≤ µ^2] reaches 1-α within target amplitude-estimation accuracy
algorithm.parameter_initialization: bisection initialized with µ_l=0 and µ_h=1; polynomial coefficients obtained by minimax optimization over Chebyshev basis

optimizer_settings.parameter_bounds: Chebyshev coefficients constrained by minimax formulation; no iterative optimizer settings reported

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Derivative pricing oracle A is treated as a block-encoding; QSP applies polynomial transformations to singular values sqrt(V(s)) across superposed scenarios
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate VaR_α[V] = V0 - µ_α^2 where µ_α is the smallest threshold such that P[V ≤ µ_α^2] ≥ 1-α
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Polynomial approximation to threshold function θ_µ(x) using QSP; QAE estimates the marked-state probability

problem_instance.description: Derivative portfolio risk estimation over multiple market scenarios; benchmarked numerically on sampled scenario prices from a normal distribution

dataset_specification.description: Scenario prices sampled from N(µ=0.5, σ^2=0.09^2) for numerical studies; benchmark averaged over µ∈[0.45,0.48,0.5,0.52,0.55]

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Scenario values normalized to [0,1]; threshold function approximated on [0,1] with even Chebyshev polynomials
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 100 independent samples per data point for numerical error plots; 200 repetitions for advantage benchmark; bisection search over µ with QAE at each step

implementation_details.classical_solver: classical Monte Carlo / sorting for baseline and comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Generate scenario prices; compute classical VaR by sorting samples
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare quantum VaR estimate to classical percentile estimate

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: bisection-based threshold search; no training loss

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Authors estimate that for N≈50k scenarios, quantum VaR could reduce required logical clock rate for advantage by up to ~30× relative to single-derivative pricing benchmarks.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Polynomial degree d ≥ ~600 and amplitude estimation accuracy ε_A ≈ 1.2×10^-3 in their numerical study; pricing oracle T-depth assumed TA ≈ 3900 (from Ref. [19]). End-to-end T-depth given by Eq. (48).
limiting_factors: Quadratic speedup only (ε^-2 vs ε^-4 scaling)
Large polynomial degree required for QSP threshold approximation
Heavy reliance on fault-tolerant logical clock rates
Assumes efficient scenario state preparation that is not yet demonstrated
Resource estimates rely on previously published derivative pricing oracle assumptions

notes: No physical QPU or simulator platform is named for the numerical experiments; treated as simulator_other because the paper reports explicit numerical simulations of the algorithm rather than hardware execution.
The paper reports oracle-call counts and an end-to-end T-depth formula, but not a concrete qubit count or compiled circuit depth for a specific benchmark instance; those remain null.
Section VII reports that VaR estimation could reduce the logical clock rate required for quantum advantage by up to ~30× relative to single-derivative pricing.
However, results are derived from numerical simulations and resource estimates rather than hardware execution.
